subject: english
question:
Select the most appropriate idiomatic expression that can substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence.:

It feels like I __made a promise of more than my ability__ when I promised to complete this worksheet in one day.

options.text: bit off more than I could chew
burnt a hole in my pocket

solution:
The correct answer is: **Option 1** i.e. **bit off more than I could chew**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The idiom **"bit off more than I could chew"** means to take on a task that is way too big or beyond one's ability to manage. (अपनी हिम्मत से ज्यादा काम करना)

 
 
• **Example:** John realized he had bitten off more than he could chew when he promised to complete the project in one week.
 
 

Therefore, the correct answer is: **Option 1 i.e. bit off more than I could chew**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

Here are the other options explained along with their Hindi meanings and example sentences:

 
• **Beat my brain out** (अपना दिमाग खराब करना): To try very hard to understand or figure out something.

 
 
• **Example:** I've been beating my brain out trying to solve this math problem.
 
 
 
• **Beat the drum** (ढोल पीटना): To promote or support something enthusiastically.
 
 
• **Example:** She is always beating the drum for environmental conservation.
 
 
 
• **Burnt a hole in my pocket** (जेब में छेद कर दिया): To spend a lot of money quickly.
 
 
• **Example:** The new video game system burnt a hole in my pocket.
